output.summary: A flowering plant native to North America, Jerusalem artichoke has rough, toothed leaves and golden-yellow flowers. It is cultivated for its edible tubers, which store inulin rather than starch and have been grown by Indigenous American peoples since before Europeans arrived.
output.edibilityNote: Its edible tubers were cultivated by Indigenous American peoples before European arrival; cooking breaks their stored inulin down into fructose.
